description: §52.8/§19.6/§17.1 — an `if=` on a tag whose emit dispatch RETURNS BEFORE the §17.1 mount gate (`<errorBoundary>`) is never applied: the boundary emits `<div data-scrml-error-boundary>` and walks its children LIVE, so the content rendered whatever the condition said. Since S469 that `if=` is REFUSED (E-GATE-UNSUPPORTED-HOST — fail closed, no artifact). The SSR half still holds: the dispatch produces no `<template>`, so NO I-SSR-EACH-CLIENT-RENDERED fires (its stated reason would be false).
rationale: g-ssr-each-under-if-blank-paint (S433 fix round) — the INVERTED defect found by adversarial review. Mirroring emit-html's `if=` gate PREDICATE (`isGateableIfValue`) is not the same as mirroring its DISPATCH: the predicate says whether the gate would accept the value, never whether control flow reaches the gate. The first cut of the fix suppressed the renderer here and emitted a lint whose reason was factually false — measured as 2 rows painted before, 0 after, at exit 0. The bypass set is derived by enumerating every `return` above the gate in emitNode's markup branch; this case fails if that mirror is dropped or if a future dispatch reorder is not carried into it. S469 (s469-structural-else-guard, g-if-on-structural-element-silently-ignored): the `if=` itself was a fail-open guard — `<errorBoundary if=@x>` painted its subtree with `@x` false — and is now refused; this case keeps the lint half and pins the refusal.
